newsitem.title: USA: Johnson Matthey unit gets U.S. incentives.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Matthey unit gets U.S. incentives.

text.p: Johnson Matthey Electronics, a unit of Britain's Johnson Matthey Plc, said it had received a $3.25 million business incentives package from Wisconsin and will invest $60 million in the state.
The company said in a statement late on Wednesday it got the package "in recognition and support of the high-tech company's commitment to growing and training the local employment base."

JME's two plants in Chippewa Falls produce and assemble laminate-based packages for semiconductor devices. They employ nearly 600 people and the company has pledged to create an additional 600 full-time positions by mid-1998.
JME also will invest about $60 million of its own funds in renovating and installing new manufacturing equipment at its Chippewa Falls plants.
The package includes income tax credits and a training grant.
